routes.label: Verify an explicit term by induction

officialSolution.label: 2019 AMC 10A

solution:
The product in the recurrence's numerator suggests taking reciprocals, which will separate the two preceding terms. Define \(b_n=1/a_n\). Then
\[
b_n=\frac{2a_{n-2}-a_{n-1}}{a_{n-2}a_{n-1}}
=\frac{2}{a_{n-1}}-\frac{1}{a_{n-2}}
=2b_{n-1}-b_{n-2}.
\]
Rearranging gives
\[
b_n-b_{n-1}=b_{n-1}-b_{n-2}.
\]
Thus the reciprocals form an arithmetic sequence. Its first two terms are \(1\) and \(7/3\), so its common difference is
\[
\frac73-1=\frac43.
\]
Therefore
\[
b_{2019}=1+2018\cdot\frac43
=\frac{3+8072}{3}
=\frac{8075}{3},
\]
and hence
\[
a_{2019}=\frac{3}{8075}.
\]
The digits of \(8075\) sum to \(20\), so \(8075\) is not divisible by \(3\). The fraction is already in lowest terms, and
\[
p+q=3+8075=\boxed{8078}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
